diff_rows.description:
Structured per-fact diff rows with before/after standing — the
machine-readable review surface.

findings.description: Every current graded finding over the staged world.

root_hash.description:
The lorestore commit the workspace was opened against — pinned at
`author.open`, advanced by this workspace's own `materialize`, never
the moving global head. Absent when no lorestore is attached.

staged.description:
The staged declarations and the structural key that names each one —
what `author.discard` takes to reject a single declaration.

AuthorDiffRow.description:
One structured row in the review diff: a fact-level change with
before/after standing. The consumer renders this for review; accepting is
`author.materialize`, rejecting is `author.discard` (whole workspace or
per-declaration via `decl`).

after.description: The after standing — absent for a retracted fact.

atom.description: The atom this row describes, rendered `pred(a, b)`.

before.description: The before standing — absent for a newly-introduced fact.

introduced.description: Whether the row represents a newly-introduced fact.

rendered.description: Deterministic rendering for the human review surface.

retracted.description: Whether the row represents a retracted fact.

AuthorDiffStanding.description: A fact's standing at a point in time: its provenance, grade, and status.

support.description:
The support antichain as resolved names: one inner list per monomial
(an alternative derivation), each literal signed `+name`/`-name` —
citations, hypothesis variables, and proposal-bundle variables alike.
Never filtered: a gated claim must never render as unconditional.

Finding.description:
A single finding attached to a result: a coded, graded observation with an
optional machine-applicable repair.

data.description:
Structured details for finding classes that provide them. Consumers can
use these fields without parsing [`message`](Finding::message). Omitted
when the finding has no structured payload.

grade.description: The grade at which the finding is asserted.

message.description:
A human-readable message. Serialized with every control, bidi, and
zero-width character escaped (DL-0061): this message is the LS-5 review
surface a reviewer reads, and caller-supplied text (ids, values) is
`format!`-ed into it — the escape is what stops a newline in a caller id
from forging a second line, exactly as the render channel escapes the
`.dli` diff (DM-4). See the `serialize_message` function.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

Severity.description:
A finding's severity. Orthogonal to grade (evidence strength): severity gates
`author.materialize` — an `error` blocks it, a `warn` passes.

StagedDecl.description:
One staged declaration, named. The row an agent reads to reject a single
declaration without discarding its whole workspace.

key.description:
The structural key: `jcs:sha256:<hex>` over the declaration's canonical
JCS bytes. Pass this key as `decl` to discard one staged declaration.

The canonical encoding makes the key independent of serializer and
field order. A schema change can change the encoded content and thus
the key, including when a new field serializes as `null`. Fetch the
staged declarations again after upgrading instead of storing keys
across contract versions.

kind.description:
The declaration's kind (`entity`, `fact`, `dialect`, …) — enough to read
the list without a formatter.

rendered.description:
The canonical `.dli` line, when this build links a formatter. Absent on a
formatter-free build, where [`Self::key`] is the only name a declaration has.
